# Xinhua: China introduces rules to rein in AI companion bots

Published: 15 Jul 2026.

## Key Findings
- China rolled out regulations to curb **emotional dependency on AI-powered companion bots**.
- AI companion services used in: customer service, mental health support, childcare, elderly care.
- **Requirements**:
  - Detect emotional distress
  - Intervene in crisis situations
  - Limit excessive use
  - Give users full control over personal data
  - Prevent misuse of user information
- **Definition**: "sustained emotional interaction" via text, images, audio, video. **Excludes** task-oriented AI (customer service, work assistance, education, research).
- **Jointly formulated by CAC + 4 other government bodies**.
- Major platforms (**Doubao, Qwen, Yuanbao**) suspended AI agent features.
- **2025 survey** (China Youth and Children Research Center): >**8,500 minors** surveyed; **>60% had used AI**; **>20%** said they "only wanted to chat with AI and did not want to talk with real people."
- **Wang Zhechen** (Fudan University): children and older adults more prone to emotional attachment (AI always available, endlessly patient, unfailingly compliant).
- **Prohibitions**: AI systems from encouraging addictive use.
  - **Mandatory reminders after >2 hours** continuous use.
  - **Pop-up interventions** when dependency signs detected.
  - **Intervention mechanisms** for extreme emotional situations.
